path_resolution: every path below is relative to the repository root (the parent directory of configs/)
hypothesis: The ranking improvement of the centered and CSZ label schemes over the raw-label reference may be partly carried by style and industry exposure. Replaying all three schemes through one frozen approximation of the official preprocessing (winsorize, standardize, previous-day equal-weight BARRA residualization) shows whether the ranking edge, long-short performance and turnover survive, and what net exposures the long-short portfolios still carry.
decision: none: this round is descriptive. No scheme, seed or threshold is selected or promoted, and no accept/reject gate is applied to any contrast.

No jyc_eval module, wheel or notebook exists in the workspace, the data-platform JSON or the official demo scripts.

The online notebook environment is not reachable from this offline checkout, and the configured web-search provider is unavailable, so the official winsorization parameters, standardization, exposure snapshot date, regression weighting and missing-value handling cannot be inspected.
official_reference.consequence: The pipeline below is a local approximation frozen before any result of this round was computed. It is not the official preprocessing and no official score is produced.

risk_model.exposure_date_rule: use the most recent exposure date strictly before the signal date (previous trading day); every one of the eight timestamps of a day uses that same snapshot; same-day rows are never used and there is no forward fill
risk_model.exposure_date_evidence: the exposure table is daily at midnight and its ret column is the same day's return: ret(date t) equals the t-1 -> t float_market_cap ratio for 98.95% of 2023 observations with median absolute difference 0. A row is therefore an end-of-day snapshot whose intraday publication time is unverified, so the previous trading day is the conservative choice.

regression.weighting: equal (ordinary least squares); the official weights column is not used
regression.industry_encoding: all 32 industry dummies (they span the intercept)
regression.label_use: the training/evaluation label never enters the residualization; only the post-residual ranking metrics read target returns

risk_model.weights_note: the official weights column sums to about 0.209 per day over the 999 evaluation names, i.e. it is normalized over a broader universe than the evaluation pool; that is one more reason not to use it as a regression weight

score_preprocess.winsorize: per timestamp, clip at median +/- 3 * 1.4826 * MAD; if MAD is zero fall back to the population standard deviation; a constant section becomes zeros
score_preprocess.invariance_note: ranking metrics are invariant to monotone transforms, so winsorization and standardization affect only the regression fit

risk_model.uncovered_stock: a stock without a previous-day exposure row is dropped from that timestamp for every scheme, seed and variant; the same exclusion applies to the raw comparison variant

sample.rule: prediction keys from the frozen scoring run, intersected with official target keys and with the previous-day exposure snapshot; the residualization fit uses prediction keys intersected with the exposure snapshot (larger by the target-missing rows) so that the fit never reads labels; ranking metrics are then computed on the common evaluated sample

cand_centered.label: label centered by the full-timestamp training mean (control)

evaluation.source: jinyiquant.evaluation local-v1, the same scorer that produced the archived research metrics

stress.volatility: a day is high-volatility when the previous trading day's cross-sectional median |ret| exceeds the median of that statistic over the 20 exposure dates strictly before that previous day
stress.volume: a day is high-volume when the previous trading day's sampled-window vwap volume exceeds the median of the daily total over the same 20 exposure dates
stress.timestamps: per-timestamp aggregates over all 20 days are reported as the different-time-of-day view

statistics.rule: daily differences are averaged across seeds, then resampled in contiguous day blocks within each window; both block lengths are reported and no block length is chosen after seeing results

access_policy: research_a and research_b only; the confirmation, locked and legacy final ranges are not read. No model is trained or refitted; only frozen predictions are re-scored.
interpretation_rule: Report raw and processed metrics side by side. A processed improvement over raw is a local signal-effect statement; a cross-scheme comparison is descriptive because these two research windows were already used for selection. Net-exposure tables are risk diagnostics, not a promotion criterion.
